active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on a fully gauge-fixed asymmetric exact-ratio formulation, seeded around the incumbent rather than using soft-extrema force continuation.
active_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a large batched continuation on soft minimum and maximum distances, then uses one SLSQP epigraph polish. Its strength is that the continuation discovers a basin with many nearly balanced short and diameter pairs, while the final constrained solve correctly targets squared minimum distance after normalizing the diameter. Its main weakness is that the high-power soft objective has discontinuous active-set changes and can collapse the population into the same near-antipodal basin before SLSQP starts. Build a 33-coordinate gauge-fixed representation with point 0 fixed at the origin, point 1 on the x axis at unit distance, and point 2 in the xy plane; include all remaining free coordinates directly. Run one deterministic scipy.optimize.differential_evolution call in tight coordinate bounds around several hardcoded high-quality incumbent geometries encoded as an initial population, with the objective equal to the exact evaluator ratio min(d2)/max(d2), not a soft surrogate. Use a large penalty only for invalid gauge geometry or near-coincident points, since DE does not need explicit pairwise inequality constraints. Preserve and return the best evaluated individual after an exact pairwise-distance recomputation. This uses DE as the sole optimization call and specifically searches for an asymmetric basin which the current antipodal-heavy population and force field may systematically miss.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The evaluator's actual primary quantity min_pairwise_squared_distance divided by max_pairwise_squared_distance; emphasize global discovery of a different contact graph rather than further soft-objective polishing of the present graph.
active_paradigms.cautions: A full unbounded 33-dimensional DE search is ineffective, so finite bounds must be derived from diameter normalization and centered on stored strong configurations. Do not append SLSQP polishing, because the proposed strategy must remain a single optimization call. Use a fixed seed, deferred/vectorized evaluation if supported, and score candidates using the exact min/max squared distances so that no square-root or surrogate-ranking mismatch is introduced.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.shgo to enumerate low-dimensional contact-family alternatives after eliminating rigid motions and imposing a selected geometric symmetry only as a search parameterization.
active_paradigms.description: The incumbent's final SLSQP phase is a local epigraph optimizer, so it can only improve the contact graph already selected by the soft descent. Instead, construct several compact low-dimensional candidate families from plausible 14-point contact graphs: represent points as orbits of a small involution or twofold rotation, while allowing orbit representatives to have independent radii and polar angles so the construction is not forced to be antipodal. For each chosen family, eliminate translation, rotation, and scale analytically by fixing a diameter pair and coordinates of one additional representative. The remaining dimension should be kept roughly below 8 to 12, permitting a single scipy.optimize.shgo call with box bounds on angles and radii. Define the objective as the negative exact squared ratio over all 91 pairs; SHGO's simplicial sampling is useful here because it can identify separated basins and report multiple local minima without relying on the current soft-extrema trajectory. Select the best family offline during development, then ship only the strongest deterministic family and one SHGO call in the final program. This is structurally different from merely perturbing all 14 coordinates: it searches alternative combinatorial contact topologies in a compact algebraic family.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escaping the incumbent's likely near-antipodal contact topology and increasing the limiting shortest-distance level while maintaining a normalized diameter of one.
active_paradigms.cautions: SHGO is unsuitable for the original 33-dimensional quotient space; the value comes entirely from aggressive geometric parameter reduction. The family must still return exactly 14 distinct finite points, and its symmetry must not accidentally prove too restrictive by enforcing unwanted equal distances. Bounds must avoid angle periodic duplicates and zero-radius orbit representatives. Do not follow SHGO with another optimizer; evaluate SHGO's returned point directly under the exact evaluator metric.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.direct as a deterministic bounded partition search in a small neighborhood of the best gauge-fixed configuration, with the exact nonsmooth ratio as its objective.
active_paradigms.description: The current high-power continuation behaves like a noisy subgradient method once only a few shortest and diameter pairs remain active, and its final SLSQP solve can stop on a single locally feasible active set. DIRECT is a different mechanism: it recursively partitions boxes and compares objective values across scales, so it can test coordinated finite moves that temporarily worsen one active pair but ultimately replace the active contact graph. Start from a hardcoded, already gauge-fixed best configuration and define bounded perturbation variables only for the degrees of freedom most likely to alter the active graph, for example 6 to 15 principal displacement modes obtained from deterministic eigenvectors of the contact-graph rigidity matrix. Reconstruct the 14 points from those modes, reapply the fixed gauge, and evaluate negative min(d2)/max(d2) exactly. Make one scipy.optimize.direct call over small but nontrivial coefficient bounds, allowing asymmetric mode amplitudes as well as symmetric ones. The mode restriction makes the partition search practical while directly attacking the present solution's weakness: local active-set locking rather than broad placement quality. Return the best point found by DIRECT after one exact normalization by its measured maximum squared distance.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Local but non-gradient exploration of the true nonsmooth evaluator objective, especially changes in which pairs determine dmin and dmax near the current score of 1.000016.
active_paradigms.cautions: DIRECT suffers strongly from dimensionality, so do not expose all point coordinates; use a deterministic low-rank mode basis derived from the incumbent's active or near-active distance graph. The perturbation box must be wide enough to cross contact-switch boundaries but narrow enough that the reduced basis remains meaningful. Avoid using the current soft force descent or a subsequent SLSQP call, since DIRECT should be the sole search operation. Recompute all 91 distances in float64 for final candidate selection because improvements at this score scale can be extremely small.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use differential evolution on a compact seven-direction angular parameterization to test globally different line-packing basins
tried_paradigms.description: The current population includes asymmetric 14-point starts, but its gradient flow is strongly attracted to the original antipodal/cubic-tetrahedral basin and may never discover a distinct contact graph. Parameterize seven unoriented unit directions by spherical angles, fixing the first direction and a rotational gauge so that only about eleven to fourteen bounded variables remain. Define the direct objective as max_{i<j}|dot(v_i,v_j)|; after optimization return the seven directions and their negatives. Invoke scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, a moderate population, deferred updating, workers=1 for reproducibility, and polish=False, so the single global call searches contact-graph topology rather than following the current soft-extrema trajectory. This objective is compact, bounded, and is exactly equivalent to the evaluator ratio within the antipodal family. Include a deterministic near-reference angular vector in the initial population if supported, while reserving the rest of that one population for broad exploration.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of maximum coherence across qualitatively different seven-line contact graphs; it can either find a genuinely better code or establish a better seed for a later independently developed exact construction.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Raw 42-coordinate differential evolution is prohibitively expensive and has redundant translation/scale/rotation modes; the reduced spherical-angle representation is essential. The max-absolute-dot objective is nonsmooth, so do not rely on the default local polishing stage. Bound runtime via maxiter and popsize, and always normalize reconstructed directions before returning them to avoid angular roundoff changing the diameter ratio.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the soft-extrema continuation with one direct constrained SLSQP solve of the epigraph formulation.
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a large batched projected-gradient search: it starts from an antipodal 7-direction code and random spherical starts, then maximizes a smooth approximation of log(dmin/dmax) while progressively increasing the soft-min/soft-max power. Its strengths are scale/translation removal, many concurrent basins, and a final near-active-set phase, which explains why it is already within about 0.1% of the reference. Its limiting weakness is that soft extrema still bias the solution toward non-active pairs and normalized fixed steps cannot enforce the true distance inequalities exactly. Parameterize 13 points after fixing one point at the origin, fix a second point on the x-axis and a third in the xy-plane to remove rigid motions, and include a scalar t. Use scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP") once on the best current configuration, maximizing t subject to every squared distance being at least t and at most 1, with the current diameter pair scaled to one initially. Supply exact analytic Jacobians for all 91 lower and upper distance constraints, tight ftol, and a generous maxiter, because this is the evaluator’s stated epigraph problem rather than a surrogate. Return the coordinate portion of the feasible solution after optionally rescaling by its measured maximum distance.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize t=(dmin/dmax)^2, exactly the evaluator’s min_max_ratio and therefore combined_score; feasibility of the active shortest-pair and diameter constraints is the priority.
tried_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP is local and the formulation is nonconvex, so initialize from the current best antipodal-search result rather than a generic random array. Do not constrain a diameter pair to equal one by assumption unless it is also represented by the all-pairs upper constraints; the actual identity of the diameter can switch. Carefully remove only rigid-motion degrees of freedom, not shape degrees of freedom, and provide finite coordinates even if SLSQP reports a mild line-search warning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic differential evolution on a gauge-fixed exact ratio objective to search asymmetric basins that the antipodal seed population may miss.
tried_paradigms.description: The existing method strongly favors antipodal configurations because half of its population is generated as perturbations of an explicitly antipodal base, and even its spherical starts are quickly attracted by the same soft-force landscape. This is efficient for finding a nearly optimal spherical-code-like arrangement, but it can miss a slightly asymmetric configuration with a better exact extreme-distance ratio. Construct a reduced 33-dimensional coordinate parameterization by fixing translation and orientation, and evaluate the exact objective min(pairwise squared distances)/max(pairwise squared distances) directly, not a power-mean surrogate. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, mutation dithering, workers=1 for reproducibility, and bounds wide enough to contain normalized configurations. Add a deterministic normalization inside the objective by centering and dividing by RMS radius before computing the ratio, so coordinate magnitude does not consume search range. Set polish=True only if its internal final local operation is acceptable in the runtime environment; otherwise rely on a sufficiently large population and iterations. This supplies genuinely global, nonsymmetric exploration rather than another temperature schedule around the same seeds.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current projected soft-extrema basin and maximize the exact squared pairwise ratio, particularly by testing whether the true 14-point optimum breaks the imposed antipodal structure.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The raw min/max objective is nonsmooth and differential evolution in 33 dimensions can be expensive, so use a realistic population/iteration budget and retain the best known configuration as one member of the initialization population if supported. Gauge fixing must not accidentally force a particular pair to be the diameter. Avoid parallel workers because evaluator import/runtime behavior and reproducibility can become unreliable.

tried_paradigms.idea: Perform an active-contact rigidity polish by solving equal-distance contact equations with a single scipy root solve.
tried_paradigms.description: Near the current score, only a small set of shortest pairs and longest pairs determines the evaluator, whereas the current high-power gradients continue to receive weak contributions from many inactive pairs. First inspect the current returned configuration deterministically and form two contact graphs using pairs within a very small relative tolerance of dmin and dmax. Fix translation, rotation, and scale with coordinate gauges, then use scipy.optimize.root once on equations that set all selected short contacts to a common squared length, all selected diameter contacts to one, and impose stationarity through contact-force equilibrium weights or a minimally determined independent subset of those equations. The goal is to move from a soft-objective stationary point to a rigid realization of the actual active contact pattern. After root convergence, verify all 91 distances and retain the root result only if its exact evaluator ratio exceeds the unpolished configuration. If the contact pattern is overdetermined, select equations using a rank-revealing QR of their numerical Jacobian so the root system is square and non-singular. This approach is qualitatively different from global search: it treats the nearly optimal geometry as a contact-framework realization problem and can recover the final missing digits once the correct graph has been found.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact gap between the active shortest-distance shell and active diameter shell; eliminate residual inequality slack or imbalance left by soft-max continuation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A root solver does not itself enforce all inactive inequalities, so always evaluate every pair after solving and reject any candidate that creates a newly shorter pair or longer diameter. Contact-set thresholds should be relative to the measured distances and conservative enough not to include clearly inactive pairs. The gauge and equation count must be consistent; otherwise singularity is expected and the original configuration should be returned.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a gauge-fixed, exact nonsmooth ratio objective to search for a genuinely asymmetric basin
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a large batched soft-extrema flow and then SLSQP polishing. Its strength is that it starts from the relevant antipodal seven-line seed and eventually optimizes the actual epigraph constraints; this explains why it reaches the reference score. Its weakness is that the high-power softmax stages and the final SLSQP call are strongly local, so they mostly preserve the seed’s contact topology and can miss a slightly better asymmetric diameter/contact graph. Replace the population continuation and SLSQP polish by one direct global call to scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a 36-dimensional gauge-fixed coordinate vector: fix point 0 at the origin, point 1 on the x-axis, and point 2 in the xy-plane. The scalar objective should be negative min(d2)/max(d2), evaluated directly from all 91 squared distances, with a large finite penalty for coincident points or numerically degenerate gauges. Use broad but finite coordinate bounds, such as [-1,1] for free coordinates, because scale is removed inside the objective by dividing by dmax. Seed x0 from the existing seven-direction construction, but let annealing use reannealing and local search to alter contact combinatorics rather than merely perturbing a known basin. Return the best normalized geometry seen by the objective, not the annealer’s nominal termination point. This is fundamentally different from the failed differential-evolution attempt because it searches the full gauge-fixed 14-point geometry rather than an antipodal seven-direction angular family.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact evaluator quantity min_pair_squared_distance / max_pair_squared_distance; prioritize discovering a contact graph different from the current near-antipodal local basin.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The raw objective is nonsmooth whenever the identity of a closest or farthest pair changes, so do not use a soft surrogate in the reported selection criterion. Keep a deterministic seed and a strict iteration/time budget. Gauge fixing must not accidentally force an incorrect orientation; choose a noncollinear third point from the seed and parameterize only its x and y entries. Since the known score is already within roughly 1.6e-5 of reference, only accept a candidate after recomputing all pairwise distances in float64 and normalizing by its actual diameter.

tried_paradigms.idea: Derive an exact low-dimensional contact-family parameterization from the observed active graph and solve it with sympy.nsolve
tried_paradigms.description: The present code already exposes the valuable clue that the solution is extremely close to a structured 14-point configuration, but its SLSQP epigraph formulation treats all 39 geometric degrees of freedom independently. Inspect the returned best configuration offline and classify edges into diameter edges, shortest-contact edges, and clearly slack edges with a tolerance around 1e-6. Use graph automorphisms of this active graph to partition vertices into symmetry orbits, then parameterize one representative coordinate per orbit and generate the full 14-point set through the inferred rotations/reflections or paired affine relations. Impose equations saying every shortest-contact edge has squared length t, every diameter edge has squared length 1, plus centroid and gauge equations; the unknowns are orbit parameters and t. Call sympy.nsolve once at high precision, for example 80 to 150 decimal digits, starting from the numerical configuration. This turns the nearly singular nonsmooth constrained optimization into solving a small equal-distance algebraic system, potentially recovering the exact reference geometry rather than a floating-point approximate stationary point. After converting the high-precision coordinates back to float64, test every non-contact edge; if all are strictly between t and 1, the solution is a valid candidate and often improves the score simply by eliminating the 1e-5-scale residual imbalance left by soft descent and SLSQP.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical precision and exact equality of the true shortest and diameter contact classes, thereby reducing residual spread that lowers the squared ratio.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This should be based on an empirically verified active graph, not an assumed antipodal symmetry: the failed KKT root approach likely failed because it solved an overdetermined or incorrectly guessed active set. Include only independent equal-distance equations, and reject the solve if any nominally slack pair violates [t,1] after normalization. High-precision symbolic/numerical solving can be slow, so keep the orbit-reduced system small and use fixed initial values derived from the deterministic seed.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.milp to select a promising diameter/contact graph before reconstructing its geometry analytically
tried_paradigms.description: The key limitation of the current continuous method is contact-topology blindness: it only discovers which pairs are active after moving coordinates. Instead, use a discrete graph screen to identify plausible optimal combinatorial skeletons. Construct binary variables for candidate shortest edges and candidate diameter edges on the 14 vertices, enforce degree patterns observed in the current solution or in nearby perturbations, require enough shortest contacts for rigidity, forbid an edge from belonging to both classes, and impose symmetry-breaking labels. Add linear incidence constraints ensuring the candidate graph is connected and that diameter edges can support the required width structure; maximize a rigidity/contact-quality surrogate such as total weighted contact degree while penalizing highly uneven vertex degrees. Use scipy.optimize.milp once to obtain the best graph under these combinatorial conditions. For each selected graph family, use its automorphism/orbit structure to write a deterministic coordinate ansatz with equal shortest and diameter lengths, rather than running another generic continuous optimizer. The value is not that MILP evaluates distances itself, but that it can force exploration of contact graphs excluded by the current antipodal initialization and can identify a smaller algebraic family suitable for exact reconstruction. This separates the discrete choice of active pairs from the continuous realization, which is precisely where softmax force descent is weakest.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exploration of alternative rigid contact and diameter graphs that could have a larger exact min/max squared-distance ratio than the current locally selected graph.
tried_paradigms.cautions: MILP alone cannot certify Euclidean realizability or optimize the ratio, so its output must be treated only as a graph hypothesis and checked by a deterministic geometric construction. Do not encode arbitrary quadratic distance constraints as linear constraints. Calibrate allowed degrees from actual near-best configurations, otherwise graph constraints may eliminate the true topology. Keep the candidate edge set sparse, for example pairs that become near-active across deterministic perturbations, to avoid a large and uninformative binary model.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.shgo on a low-dimensional non-antipodal symmetry-orbit model inferred from the current near-optimal code
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first performs a large batched soft-min/soft-max force continuation from an antipodal seven-line seed and random spherical starts, then applies a gauge-fixed SLSQP epigraph polish. Its strength is that the final SLSQP exactly represents the evaluator’s all-pairs constraints, which explains why it reaches the reference value; its weakness is that the force stages are expensive and the final solve is confined to whichever active-contact basin they happened to discover. Inspect the best candidate’s sorted distance rows and identify repeated point signatures and distance-equivalent point orbits, without assuming central inversion because the successful asymmetric search indicates that antipodality can be restrictive. Hard-code the resulting finite permutation-orbit ansatz: one 3-vector representative per orbit plus only those scalar parameters required by the stabilizer, then generate all 14 points by the fixed orthogonal actions. Make one scipy.optimize.shgo call on the exact evaluator quantity min(d2)/max(d2), with bounded orbit coordinates and a deterministic Sobol sampling budget. This turns the otherwise 33-dimensional nonsmooth problem into a small global search over a geometrically justified family, while retaining the asymmetric degrees of freedom absent from the failed antipodal SLSQP formulation. Return the best orbit-generated coordinates directly from SHGO rather than doing a later local polish.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The squared evaluator ratio min pairwise squared distance divided by maximum pairwise squared distance; focus on escaping the current active-contact basin while preserving likely discrete symmetry.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not use the original 7-line antipodal parameterization, since that structural restriction was explicitly unsuccessful. SHGO is only realistic after genuine orbit reduction, ideally about 4–8 free scalars; applying it to unrestricted 33-coordinate geometry is not viable. Compute the exact min(d2)/max(d2) in the objective, guard against zero diameter, and use generous coordinate bounds consistent with a centered, unit-radius representation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.direct as a deterministic basin search on the exact nonsmooth ratio in a gauge-fixed local box around several known contact topologies
tried_paradigms.description: The present implementation already demonstrates that the important issue is selecting the right active shortest and diameter pairs: its high-power soft objective is only a proxy, and SLSQP can only refine the selected basin. Replace that proxy-driven basin selection with a single DIRECT global partitioning call on a gauge-fixed coordinate chart. Fix translation and rotation by setting one point to zero, a selected putative diameter partner to (1,0,0), and one noncollinear point in the xy-plane; encode the remaining coordinates directly. Use a contact topology taken from the current returned best candidate to select the labeling and set a compact deterministic box around that geometry, but score every box point with the true all-91-pair value min(d2)/max(d2), not with contact equations or a soft surrogate. scipy.optimize.direct repeatedly subdivides promising rectangles, so it can discover coordinated finite moves that normalized gradient forces miss when several active edges must exchange status simultaneously. Unlike differential evolution, this is deterministic and does not rely on a population collapsing around the initial antipodal family. The returned DIRECT point itself is the final construction, so this is a single direct optimization rather than a continuation followed by polishing.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Gain beyond the current 1.000016 score by finding a neighboring asymmetric contact arrangement with a larger true squared ratio, especially one requiring simultaneous movement of several points.
tried_paradigms.cautions: DIRECT has no nonlinear constraint interface, so use the ratio directly rather than the SLSQP epigraph constraints; the ratio is scale invariant and remains well-defined after rejecting near-zero diameters. A full 33-dimensional box is impractical: use the Euclidean gauge and narrow bounds motivated by the current candidate/contact topology. Verify the final result with raw pdist-equivalent squared distances because a presumed fixed diameter edge may cease to be the actual diameter during search.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a spherical angular parameterization seeded by a literal asymmetric incumbent
tried_paradigms.description: The current batched force descent has broad random coverage but its normalized force is strongly biased toward smooth spherical-code basins and becomes a subgradient-like local walk at high powers. Construct all 14 points from angular variables on a common sphere, fixing three angular gauges to remove global rotation, and use the exact squared ratio min(d2)/max(d2 as the sole objective. Seed scipy.optimize.dual_annealing with a literal stored copy of the current best asymmetric point set converted to angles, rather than regenerating it through the long force-continuation pipeline. Use periodic angle handling by mapping azimuth variables into a fixed interval and use polar angles away from singular endpoints; the objective may internally reconstruct Cartesian coordinates but must always evaluate all 91 pairs. Annealing’s acceptance of temporarily worse configurations is appropriate for crossing contact-graph barriers where an improvement requires first reducing a currently nonactive distance. This is fundamentally different from the failed differential-evolution population search and from active-contact root solving: it searches the true nonsmooth objective through thermal barrier crossing, with no assumed active graph. Make the annealing result the returned point set, retaining the incumbent whenever its directly measured ratio is higher.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The primary evaluator squared ratio, with emphasis on asymmetric basins and contact-graph changes that cannot be reached by the present final sharp force stages.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a fixed seed and a finite iteration/evaluation cap suitable for the timeout. Do not add a subsequent SLSQP or root polish, since the candidate should be evaluated and returned directly. Angular parameterization has pole degeneracies; either fix a gauge point away from the poles or represent each point with bounded stereographic coordinates to avoid duplicate coordinate descriptions. Always compare the annealed candidate against the stored incumbent using the evaluator’s min(d2)/max(d2), not a smoothed energy.
